evidence.source_sentence: Chemical structure of aerogels was studied qualitatively by FTIR spectroscopy, as presented in Figure 7.

The characteristic bands of polyimides, including 727 ( cm-1), $1 3 7 0 ( \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 } )$(imide C−N), 1715 $( \mathsf { c m } ^ { - 1 } )$(symmetric imide C=O) and $1 7 7 5 ( \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 } )$(asymmetric imide C=O) are observed for all studied samples.

The characteristic bands of polyimides, including 727 ( cm-1), $1 3 7 0 ( \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 } )$(imide C−N), 1715 $( \mathsf { c m } ^ { - 1 } )$(symmetric imide C=O) and $1 7 7 5 ( \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 } )$(asymmetric imide C=O) are observed for all studied samples.

However, PMDA backbone aerogels presented small peaks at 1660 $\textstyle { \left( \cos ^ { - 1 } \right) }$(amic acid C=O) and $1 5 3 5 \ : \mathrm { ~ ( ~ c m } ^ { - 1 } )$(amide C−N) bands, which may suggest incomplete imidization of polyimide samples.

characterizations.result_summary: Glass transition temperature of polyimide aerogels was observed in the range of 250 °C to 300 °C, with barely observable peaks in samples with higher PPDA and/or PMDA content.

evidence.source_sentence: As presented in Figure 9, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) test was performed on fabricated aerogels. Due to highly crosslink nature of fabricated aerogels, the glass transition peak was barely observed in some of the samples; and specifically, for those with higher PPDA and/or PMDA content. In overall, the glass transition in range of $2 5 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$to $3 0 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$was observed.
Figure 9. The DSC results of A) PMDA and, B) BPDA backbone aerogels with varying diamine fraction.
